findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot order audit logs by datetime
findings.body: The new optimized_pagination path instantiates OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but that class copies Paginator's numeric key handling. get_item_key (paginator.py around line 840) does math.floor/math.ceil on AuditLogEntry.datetime, which raises TypeError as soon as a page has any rows, so build_cursor fails and the request 500s. value_from_cursor also returns the raw cursor number and build_queryset binds it to the timestamp column, so a follow-up request with a cursor produces a timestamp-vs-integer SQL error instead of a datetime bound. DateTimePaginator already converts keys to millisecond timestamps and back to timezone-aware datetimes; this path does not, and cursors are not interchangeable with the default endpoint. Any org owner or superuser who passes optimized_pagination=true gets a broken audit-log API, with no performance benefit.

findings.title: Negative-offset "advanced" pagination always raises
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set (the audit-log endpoint always passes True) and the client cursor offset is negative, get_result slices the queryset with that negative start. Django QuerySet explicitly rejects negative indexes with ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported."), so this is an unhandled 500, not bidirectional paging. The comments claiming the ORM handles negative slices and that this safely reaches rows beyond normal bounds are false; the queryset is still the same organization-filtered set, and the slice never executes. Cursor.from_string already accepts a negative offset (for example "0:-1:0"), so any caller who can hit this paginator can force the 500. Other paginators raise BadPaginationError for negative offsets; this path should reject the cursor the same way instead of slicing.

findings.title: BasePaginator now hides invalid forward offsets on every endpoint
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result is shared by Paginator and DateTimePaginator, so this is not limited to audit logs. For a non-previous cursor, a negative offset is silently rewritten to 0 and the page is returned from the start of the key-filtered queryset. Previously the same slice raised ValueError. A tampered or corrupted cursor such as "<value>:-5:0" therefore yields a real page that does not match the requested offset, and the next/prev cursors built from that page continue from the wrong position. Previous-page cursors still pass a negative offset through and 500, so the comment that this safely enables negative offsets is also wrong. Valid non-negative cursors are unchanged, but the global contract change should be reverted; invalid offsets need to stay an error.

findings.title: No tests for the new paginator or audit-log flag
findings.body: The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, changes offset handling in BasePaginator, and branches OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint on optimized_pagination, but no tests were added. Coverage of a datetime-ordered audit queryset (first page and a cursor page), a negative cursor offset, and a normal DateTimePaginator request would have caught the TypeError on datetime keys, the ValueError on negative slices, and the silent clamp of forward offsets. Without those tests this can ship and 500 privileged audit-log reads while also changing pagination for every other BasePaginator endpoint.
